bookTitle: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets

facts.statement: Reversal patterns mark major transition phases where shifts in supply and demand reverse the prevailing trend over long build durations, whereas continuation patterns represent shorter-term intermediate pauses that digest overbought or oversold conditions before resuming the original trend.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Major Reversal Patterns: Rules & Head and Shoulders
sourceCitation.excerpt: Reversal Patterns: Price formations that indicate a major change... Continuation Patterns: Formations that indicate the market is merely pausing

facts.statement: A well-established prior trend is an absolute prerequisite for any valid reversal formation; if a price structure resembling a reversal pattern emerges without a preceding trend to reverse, the formation is technically suspect and invalid.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Major Reversal Patterns: Rules & Head and Shoulders
sourceCitation.excerpt: A prerequisite for any reversal pattern is a well-established prior trend... if a pattern appears without a prior trend, it is suspect

facts.statement: The initial technical signal of an impending trend reversal is frequently the violation of a major trendline, which indicates a shift in trend dynamics that may lead either to an immediate reversal or a sideways consolidation phase.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Major Reversal Patterns: Rules & Head and Shoulders
sourceCitation.excerpt: The first signal of an impending trend reversal is often the violation of a major trendline.

facts.statement: The magnitude of the subsequent price move following pattern completion correlates directly with the pattern's physical dimensions, where vertical height measures price volatility and horizontal width reflects the time duration required to build the structure.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Major Reversal Patterns: Rules & Head and Shoulders
sourceCitation.excerpt: The larger the price pattern (measured in vertical height and horizontal width/duration), the greater the subsequent move.

facts.statement: Topping formations develop faster with wider, more violent price swings and higher volatility, whereas bottoming formations exhibit narrower price ranges and require significantly longer time durations to build, making bottoms less costly and less treacherous to trade.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Major Reversal Patterns: Rules & Head and Shoulders
sourceCitation.excerpt: Tops Are Shorter and More Volatile... Bottoms Have Smaller Price Ranges and Take Longer

facts.statement: While market tops can collapse of their own weight due to buyer inertia without heavy downside volume, upside breakouts from bottoming patterns strictly require a significant expansion in trading volume to validate the reversal.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Major Reversal Patterns: Rules & Head and Shoulders
sourceCitation.excerpt: While market tops can 'fall of their own weight'... upside breakouts at bottoms must be accompanied by a significant expansion in volume

facts.statement: The Head and Shoulders Top is the most reliable major reversal pattern, characterized by three distinct peaks where the central peak (the head) exceeds the altitude of the two surrounding peaks (the left and right shoulders).

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Major Reversal Patterns: Rules & Head and Shoulders
sourceCitation.excerpt: The Head and Shoulders Top is recognized as the best known and most reliable of all major reversal patterns. It consists of three distinct peaks

facts.statement: Following a heavy-volume Left Shoulder rally (Peak A) and light-volume pullback (Point B), the Head (Peak C) rallies to a higher high on noticeably lighter volume, followed by a decline to Point D that penetrates below Peak A.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Major Reversal Patterns: Rules & Head and Shoulders
sourceCitation.excerpt: Prices rally to a new high (Peak C), but volume is noticeably lighter... The subsequent decline (Point D) penetrates below Peak A

facts.statement: The Right Shoulder (Peak E) forms via a third rally on noticeably light volume that fails to reach the altitude of the Head (Peak C), establishing the descending peak sequence required for a trend reversal.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Major Reversal Patterns: Rules & Head and Shoulders
sourceCitation.excerpt: Right Shoulder (Peak E): A third rally occurs on noticeably light volume but fails to reach the height of Peak C.

facts.statement: The neckline is drawn connecting the two intervening reaction troughs (Points B and D); at market tops it normally slopes upward, though it can be horizontal or downward-slanting, the latter signaling severe weakness but yielding a late sell signal.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Major Reversal Patterns: Rules & Head and Shoulders
sourceCitation.excerpt: Neckline Definition: A trendline drawn underneath the two intervening reaction lows (troughs B and D)... Upward Slanting: Most common at tops

facts.statement: A Head and Shoulders Top is not complete until price decisively breaks the neckline on a closing basis, validated by either a 1% to 3% price penetration filter or the two-day rule requiring two consecutive daily closes below the neckline.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Major Reversal Patterns: Rules & Head and Shoulders
sourceCitation.excerpt: Technicians apply price filters such as a 1% to 3% closing penetration... The 'two-day rule' requires two consecutive daily closes below the broken neckline

facts.statement: If a Head and Shoulders neckline rests at a price level of 100.00, applying Murphy's 1% to 3% price filter and two-day time filter requires the asset to close between 99.00 and 97.00 or lower across two consecutive daily sessions to confirm the breakdown.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Major Reversal Patterns: Rules & Head and Shoulders
sourceCitation.excerpt: Price Filters: Technicians apply price filters such as a 1% to 3% closing penetration beyond the neckline. Time Filters: The 'two-day rule' requires two consecutive daily closes

facts.statement: After an initial neckline breakdown, prices often execute a low-volume return move back to the underside of the broken neckline or reaction low D, which reverses roles from prior support to overhead resistance before heavy volume resumes the downtrend.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Major Reversal Patterns: Rules & Head and Shoulders
sourceCitation.excerpt: The broken neckline and reaction low D reverse roles from prior support to overhead resistance... The return move itself must take place on light volume

facts.statement: The probability of a return move is inversely related to initial breakdown volume: very heavy volume on the neckline break diminishes the chance of a bounce due to strong downside momentum, whereas lighter breakdown volume makes a return move highly likely.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Major Reversal Patterns: Rules & Head and Shoulders
sourceCitation.excerpt: If the initial neckline breakdown occurs on very heavy volume, the likelihood of a return move is diminished... on lighter volume, a return move is much more likely

facts.statement: Once the neckline is broken, prices must not close back above it; a decisive close back inside the neckline invalidates the breakdown as a false signal (Failed Head and Shoulders) and indicates the original uptrend is resuming.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Major Reversal Patterns: Rules & Head and Shoulders
sourceCitation.excerpt: A decisive close back inside the neckline signals a pattern failure ('Failed Head and Shoulders'), indicating that the initial breakdown was a false signal

generalAssumptions: Market action discounts all known and unknown fundamentals.
Prices move in trends, and a trend in motion is more likely to continue than to reverse.
Chart patterns reflect the recurring psychology of market participants through supply and demand shifts.
